title: fix: skill-evolution pipeline never produced a deployable, content-changed skill
body:
## What

Two bugs in the skill-evolution pipeline that together meant it never actually produced a deployable, content-changed skill:

1. `skill_structure` constraint check ran against the stripped skill *body* instead of the reassembled artifact (frontmatter + body), so it failed on every single run regardless of whether the produced skill was valid.
2. `SkillModule` passed skill text as a DSPy `InputField` *value* rather than a `Signature`'s instructions. GEPA/MIPROv2 only mutate signature instructions and few-shot demos — they never rewrite an input field's runtime value — so `optimized_module.skill_text` was always identical to the baseline, even when the optimizer reported a real score improvement. The `dspy.GEPA(...)` constructor call also had a stale kwarg (`max_steps`, which doesn't exist) and no `reflection_lm`, so it always raised and silently fell back to MIPROv2 — which made bug #2 doubly invisible, since MIPROv2 never touches `skill_text` either.

## Why

Confirmed against real runs (Sep 11, 18, 25) that each produced a scored candidate and got rejected solely on `skill_structure`, even though the saved `evolved_FAILED.md` had valid frontmatter. Fixing #1 alone exposed #2: a fixed-frontmatter run "passed" constraints and reported +1.6% holdout improvement, but `diff baseline_skill.md evolved_skill.md` showed zero byte difference — the reported improvement was measuring a better-tuned DSPy evaluation harness, not a better skill.

## Fix

- `validate_all` takes an optional `full_text` param; `_check_skill_structure` runs against it (falls back to `artifact_text` for non-skill types). Both call sites in `evolve_skill.py` now pass the actual full file text.
- `SkillModule.skill_text` is now `predictor.predict.signature.instructions` — read live from the predictor, so it reflects whatever the optimizer actually mutated.
- Fixed the `dspy.GEPA(...)` call (`max_metric_calls` + `reflection_lm` instead of the invalid `max_steps`).
- `skill_fitness_metric` accepts GEPA's 5-arg feedback signature (`pred_name`, `pred_trace`), staying MIPRO-compatible via defaults.

## Verification

```
$ python -m pytest tests/ -q --tb=short
149 passed in ~1s
```

Added regression tests pinning both bugs:
- `test_body_only_artifact_uses_full_text_for_structure_check` — body-only text must fail structure check; passing `full_text` with valid frontmatter must pass.
- `TestSkillModuleOptimizability` — asserts `skill_text` lives on `signature.instructions` and updates when a signature is replaced (exactly what GEPA/MIPROv2 do internally).

Ran a full live evolution cycle end-to-end against `github-code-review` with the fix applied: GEPA actually executed this time (no MIPROv2 fallback), produced a substantively rewritten skill body (new sections, not a no-op), and the constraint gate correctly rejected that particular candidate for exceeding the size/growth budget — a legitimate rejection on real content, not a phantom one.

## Not in this PR

Didn't touch GEPA's reflection budget/instruction-size tuning — the live run above shows GEPA can now overshoot the size constraint on a real optimization, which is an expected outcome some fraction of the time now that content is actually changing, not something this PR needs to solve.

title: Fix/dspy 3.4 compat and skill evolution
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 cannot complete a run on the current DSPy release, and when it does
finish it silently changes nothing. This fixes the pipeline end to end and
adds the honesty gates `PLAN.md` already requires.

Built on and aligned with the diagnosis in #184 and #188: `SkillModule` held the
skill in a plain attribute, so GEPA — which seeds its candidate space from
`pred.signature.instructions` — rewrote the signature docstring instead of the
skill, and `evolved_skill.md` came back byte-identical to the baseline. I adopted
their `skill_text`-as-property shape and the full-text validator rather than
inventing a third variant.

## What this PR changes

**Runnability (dspy 3.x)**

- `dspy.GEPA` no longer takes `max_steps`. `build_gepa_optimizer()` introspects
  the installed DSPy and uses `max_metric_calls` (the unit that actually bounds
  cost), falling back to `max_full_evals`/`max_steps`, and refuses to start an
  unbounded run if no budget knob exists.
- DSPy 3.x invokes a metric with five positional args
  `(gold, pred, trace, pred_name, pred_trace)` and probes the signature at
  construction. `make_gepa_metric()` adapts any three-arg repo metric to that
  shape without changing its scoring.
- GEPA asserts on a missing reflection LM, which previously made reflective
  mutation a no-op. The factory now passes one through.
- The MIPROv2 fallback is removed: its API drifted too, so that path only ever
  turned a clear error into a confusing `ImportError`. `optuna` moves into
  `dependencies` for users of other DSPy optimizers.

**Write-back and validation**

- The skill text lives in the predictor's instructions, read back through the
  `skill_text` property, so `evolved_skill.md` is the optimizer's output rather
  than a stale attribute. (Shape from #184/#188.)
- `ConstraintValidator.validate_skill(body, frontmatter=…, baseline_body=…)`
  reassembles internally, so `skill_structure` runs against the full artifact
  and passing a bare body is no longer possible. `validate_all()` also takes an
  explicit `full_text`. (Addresses #93/#113/#114/#161/#169/#171/#175.)

**Honesty gates**

- `make_llm_judge_metric()` wires the already-implemented but never-called
  `LLMJudge` in as the default fitness. The shipped `skill_fitness_metric` is a
  keyword-overlap heuristic (`0.3 + 0.7 * word_overlap`), so optimising it
  rewards echoing the rubric rather than behaving better; on a real run it
  reported +54% while the holdout delta was 0.0. The judge scores
  correctness / procedure_following / conciseness and receives the skill text,
  and falls back to the heuristic on provider errors rather than zeroing a
  rollout (which would starve GEPA's reflective step). `--legacy-metric`
  restores the old signal. *Note: #25 and #137 also propose an LLM judge; this
  implements it as an adapter over the existing class rather than a rewrite.*
- Results are gated on `--min-improvement` (default 10%, the threshold PLAN.md
  sets) instead of declaring a win on any positive delta. Relative change,
  the threshold, and pass/fail are recorded in `metrics.json`. (#135, #16.)
- Rejected candidates are written as `evolved_FAILED_<timestamp>.md` so a later
  run cannot overwrite the previous rejected variant. (#176.)
- `output/` is gitignored: it holds the user's own skill text.

## Verification

- 162 tests pass (145 pre-existing + 17 new covering the budget knob, metric
  arity, reflection LM, judge composite/fallback, and the property-based
  write-back path).
- End-to-end on `preflight-resources` (20 synthetic examples, 10/5/5 split):
  run completes with `skill_structure` passing, and the significance gate
  correctly reports the candidate as *not* meeting the threshold rather than
  claiming a win. A keyword-overlap run on the same input had reported a
  fabricated improvement.

## Notes

Four independent API drifts here have each been proposed separately upstream
(#13, #35, #48, #73, #91, #109, #155, #159 for the DSPy side; #7, #23, #50, #95,
#97, #113, #114, #161, #173, #185, #187 for the validator). This bundles them
because none of them alone leaves Phase 1 able to run.

title: fix: make GEPA actually run + add semantic-preservation guardrail
body:
## Summary

This branch fixes the Phase 1 skill-evolution pipeline so it actually runs, and adds the one guardrail PLAN.md promised but never implemented. Each commit was verified against real command output; 220 tests pass (`pytest tests/ -q`).

The pipeline upstream currently: (a) scores with an inverted lexical-overlap metric, (b) never actually invokes the LLM judge, (c) silently falls back to MIPROv2 because GEPA's budget param was renamed in DSPy 3.4.0, and (d) has no way to import Codex session history. This branch addresses all four and adds the missing semantic-preservation guardrail.

## What changed

| Commit | What / why |
|---|---|
| `feat(importers)` | Codex session-history importer (`~/.codex/thread_history_1.sqlite`), read-only, with secret-bearing and injected-context filtering. Upstream imports Claude Code / Copilot / Hermes only. |
| `fix(fitness)` | Replace `0.3 + 0.7 * lexical_overlap` with the actual `LLMJudge` composite. The lexical proxy was inverted — keyword-stuffed nonsense scored 0.742 vs 0.374 for a good answer. |
| `test(judge)` | `judge_bakeoff.py` harness: measures discrimination and scepticism of a judge model against held-out pairs. |
| `fix(router)` | Make a local codex-router usable as the DSPy backend (Responses API, `openai/` prefix, no auth header). |
| `perf(relevance)` | Relevance scoring was a serial 150-call loop; now a 12-worker pool. Router throughput 0.25 → 1.53 calls/s. |
| `fix(optimizer)` | GEPA was never constructed: `max_steps` was renamed in DSPy 3.4.0 and the blanket `except` swallowed the TypeError into a silent MIPROv2 fallback. Introspects the installed signature instead. |
| `fix(gepa)` | Two more constructor-time failures: GEPA asserts on `reflection_lm` (was unset), and requires a 5-arg metric (ours was 3). Also adds a preflight so these fail in seconds, not after a 15-minute dataset build. |
| `feat(constraints)` | **Semantic-preservation gate (PLAN.md guardrail #4).** Documented in the plan, absent from code. Deterministic content-vocabulary retention: an evolved body must keep ≥50% of the baseline's ≥4-char terms. Catches the drift where a gate-evidence skill was rewritten into an app-reverse-engineering prompt (3% retention → rejected; a legit same-domain edit → 100% → accepted). |

## Test coverage added

- `tests/core/test_codex_importer.py` — importer (18 tests)
- `tests/core/test_fitness_judge.py` — LLM judge metric + lexical-overlap regression guard (15)
- `tests/core/test_gepa_optimizer.py`, `test_gepa_metric_arity.py`, `test_optimizer_preflight.py` — GEPA construction contract
- `tests/core/test_relevance_parallel.py`, `test_relevance_rubric.py` — concurrency + relevance rubric
- `tests/core/test_semantic_preservation.py` — the new guardrail (11)

**Total: 220 passing.**

## Not claimed

- No end-to-end skill *improvement* number. The pipeline now runs GEPA genuinely, but a trustworthy before/after delta needs a clean eval dataset, which in turn needs the relevance-rubric fix (`test_relevance_rubric.py`) to produce on-target examples. This branch makes the machinery correct; it does not assert that a specific skill got better.
- The Codex importer was validated on this machine's history only (590 pairs, 54 sessions).

## Notes for reviewers

- Guardrail #5 (human review, never direct commit) is respected — this is a PR, not a push to `main`.
- `_check_semantic_preservation` is intentionally a cheap deterministic term-retention gate, not embeddings or an LLM call — those are the slow/timing-out/non-deterministic layers that already caused trouble in the scoring path, and a drift this gross loses domain vocabulary almost entirely.

title: fix: validate reassembled skill artifact, not the frontmatter-less body
body:
## Problem

Every run of the skill evolution pipeline ended with `evolved_FAILED.md` for every skill, regardless of optimizer quality. Root cause:

`evolve_skill.py` validated `evolved_body` — the markdown body with the YAML frontmatter stripped — against the `skill_structure` constraint, which requires the text to start with `---` and contain `name:`/`description:` fields. A frontmatter-less body can never pass that check, so validation failed deterministically on every run and the pipeline never reached the holdout evaluation or produced `metrics.json`.

## Fix

- Validate the **reassembled full skill** (preserved frontmatter + evolved body) after optimization; the baseline is validated against the full raw file, so the growth check compares full-vs-full.
- `skill_fitness_metric`: accept GEPA's 5-arg metric signature `(gold, pred, trace, pred_name, pred_trace)`.
- GEPA: use `max_full_evals` (current DSPy API) instead of the removed `max_steps`.

## Verification

```
./batch-evolve.sh --model openrouter/google/gemini-2.5-flash --iterations 3 --skills 'requesting-code-review'
```

- All 4 constraints pass (size 8,741/15,000, growth +0.0%, non-empty, structure)
- Holdout evaluation runs: baseline 0.334 → evolved 0.393 (+17.5%)
- `metrics.json` + `evolved_skill.md` produced under `output/<skill>/<timestamp>/`
- `tests/core/test_constraints.py` + `tests/skills/test_skill_module.py`: 23 passed

title: fix: validate the reassembled skill so the structure gate can pass
body:
Found while running the Phase 1 skill evolution end-to-end: **every evolved variant fails the `skill_structure` gate unconditionally**, because the validator receives the evolved body alone while only the reassembled skill carries YAML frontmatter.

## Evidence (reproduced on a 3-iteration run, dspy 3.4.0)

Optimization completed in 183.4s. `size_limit`, `growth_limit` and `non_empty` all passed, then `skill_structure` failed with:

> Skill missing: YAML frontmatter (---), name field, description field

Yet the saved `output/<skill>/evolved_FAILED.md` demonstrably **has** valid frontmatter — because `evolve_skill.py` reassembles it at line 214 (`evolved_full = reassemble_skill(skill["frontmatter"], evolved_body)`) and then validates `evolved_body` instead of `evolved_full`.

The same flaw applies to the baseline validation, which validates `skill["body"]` and therefore always prints *"Baseline skill has constraint violations — proceeding anyway"*.

## Fix

- The evolved validation receives `evolved_full` — the artifact that would actually deploy.
- The baseline validation receives `skill["raw"]` — the full original file.
- `baseline_text` comparisons use the raw original so growth limits compare like against like.

The gate still rejects genuinely malformed output — it just stops rejecting every variant regardless of quality.

title: fix: make the skill evolution loop actually evolve and deploy
body:
Three bugs made Phase 1 a silent no-op end to end. Found by running the pipeline against a real skill (`gif-search`) with a live model rather than mocks.

## Bugs fixed

1. **GEPA never mutated the skill text.** `SkillModule` passed skill text as an `InputField`, but GEPA's search space is `pred.signature.instructions` (`gepa.py:140`, `:654`). `optimized_module.skill_text` silently equaled the baseline. The skill text is now set via `Signature.with_instructions` and exposed as a live property read from the inner `Predict`.
2. **Every run aborted at validation.** `evolve()` validated the stripped body with `skill_structure`, which requires the YAML frontmatter `load_skill` removes. Validation now runs on the raw full file.
3. **Metric signature rejected by DSPy 3.4.** `skill_fitness_metric` had 3 args; GEPA requires `(gold, pred, trace, pred_name, pred_trace)`. Also wired `reflection_lm` to `optimizer_model` (previously accepted and ignored) and the `run_pytest` gate (`run_test_suite` existed but was never called).

## Additions

- `make_lm()` honors `HERMES_EVOLVE_API_BASE` / `HERMES_EVOLVE_API_KEY` so runs can target any OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of hardcoded OpenAI.
- `--dataset-size` CLI flag (cost control for $2-10 runs).
- `optuna` added to dev extras — the MIPROv2 fallback imported it but never declared it.

## Verification

- 148 tests pass (`pytest tests/ -q`), including 3 new regression tests that fail against the old code.
- Full GEPA run on `gif-search` (2 iterations, live model via local OpenAI-compatible endpoint) completes: all 4 constraints pass, metrics.json written, holdout evaluated. GEPA kept the baseline when no mutation improved the score — correct optimizer behavior, not a no-op.

Happy to split this into separate PRs if preferred.

title: fix(skills): seed skill text as predictor instructions so optimizers actually evolve it
body:
## Problem

`SkillModule` stored the skill text as a plain instance attribute, but DSPy optimizers (GEPA / MIPROv2) only discover and mutate the `signature.instructions` of `named_predictors()`. Consequences:

1. **The evolved artifact always equals the baseline.** Step 6 reads back `optimized_module.skill_text`, which the optimizer never touched — a 0-line diff between `baseline_skill.md` and `evolved_skill.md`, even when holdout score improves. The improvement lives in the optimizer's generic ChainOfThought instructions, which are thrown away when saving the artifact.
2. **GEPA silently degrades to MIPROv2 at construction.** `dspy.GEPA` validates the metric signature (must accept five args `(gold, pred, trace, pred_name, pred_trace)`) and raises a `TypeError` on the three-arg `skill_fitness_metric`, so every run falls into the MIPROv2 fallback.

## Fix

- **Seed the skill text as the predictor's initial instructions** (`TaskWithSkill.with_instructions(skill_text)`). GEPA's seed candidate and `build_program` both operate on `signature.instructions` of named predictors, so the skill text becomes the component GEPA reflects on and rewrites.
- **Add `SkillModule.evolved_text()`** to read the mutated text back from the predictor, and use it in the extraction step (with a fallback for pre-change modules).
- **Add `gepa_metric()`** — a five-argument adapter around the existing keyword-overlap metric — and construct `dspy.GEPA(metric=gepa_metric, auto="light", reflection_lm=dspy.LM(optimizer_model))`. GEPA now runs natively instead of falling back.

## Verification

- Unit-level: seeded instructions are visible via `named_predictors()`; after `with_instructions()` rewrite, `evolved_text()` returns the mutated text; forward pass unaffected.
- End-to-end: ran the full pipeline against a real skill with a GLM backend — GEPA (not the fallback) executes, and the saved artifact now carries the optimizer-mutated instructions instead of a byte-identical copy of the baseline.

## Notes

- MIPROv2's win may come from few-shot demos rather than instructions; those demos are still not captured in the saved artifact. That's a separate design question (this PR keeps the artifact = instructions, matching the repo's current intent).
- `max_steps` → `auto="light"` + `reflection_lm` follows current dspy 3.4 API (`max_metric_calls` and `auto` are mutually exclusive).

title: fix(evolution): route DSPy/litellm LLM calls through OpenAI-compatible proxy
body:
## Summary
- Add `make_lm()` in `evolution/core/config.py`: builds a `dspy.LM` that honors `OPENAI_API_BASE`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` when set, routing calls through an OpenAI-compatible proxy (e.g. OpenRouter) instead of requiring direct OpenAI access.
- Add `_install_litellm_shim()`: some proxied models (e.g. `tencent/hy3:free`) reject the JSON-schema `response_format` DSPy's adapter forces; the shim intercepts `litellm.completion` for those models, drops the unsupported kwarg, calls the proxy via the `openai` client, and returns a litellm-compatible `ModelResponse`.
- Switch default `optimizer_model`/`eval_model`/`judge_model` from `openai/gpt-4.1(-mini)` to `tencent/hy3:free` so the tool works out of the box against a proxy key with no direct OpenAI access.
- Replace direct `dspy.LM(...)` construction with `make_lm(...)` in `dataset_builder.py`, `external_importers.py`, `fitness.py`, and `evolve_skill.py` so every LLM call goes through the same routing path.

## Motivation
In environments where only an OpenAI-compatible proxy key (e.g. OpenRouter) is available and there's no direct OpenAI API access, the hardcoded `openai/gpt-4.1` defaults caused every call to fail with 401. This makes the model source configurable via standard `OPENAI_API_BASE`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` env vars.

## Test Plan
- [x] Reviewed diff for correctness; changes are additive/config-only, no behavior change when `OPENAI_API_BASE`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` are unset (falls back to plain `dspy.LM(model)`)
- [ ] CI

title: feat(skills): --skill-path to evolve any skill on disk; fix GEPA wiring
body:
## Problem
`evolve_skill` could only evolve skills found inside the hermes-agent repo, so skills elsewhere on the machine could not be evaluated. Running a real evolution also exposed that the optimizer never actually changed the skill (evolved always equalled baseline) and that GEPA failed on current DSPy.

## Solution
Add an optional `--skill-path` (a `SKILL.md` file or its folder, anywhere on disk). Fix the optimizer wiring so the skill text is really what gets optimized, and run constraint checks on the full skill file.

## Changes
- `evolve_skill.py`: new `--skill-path`; `--skill` optional (one of the two required); display falls back to the full path for skills outside the repo.
- `evolve_skill.py`: GEPA call updated for current DSPy (`max_metric_calls`, `reflection_lm`, 5-arg metric wrapper).
- `skill_module.py`: skill body is now the predictor's signature instructions (the text GEPA mutates); `skill_text` reads it back.
- Constraints validated on full skill text so `skill_structure` sees frontmatter.
- New tests: `tests/skills/test_evolve_skill_path.py`, `SkillModule` test.

## Evidences
### 1. Functional End-to-End Validation
- Real CLI, skill outside repo (`~/AppData/Local/hermes/shared-skills/ship`), `--dry-run --hermes-repo <other repo>`: exit 0, `Loaded: .../ship/SKILL.md`, `Name: ship`, `DRY RUN - setup validated successfully`.
- Real CLI, missing path: exit 1, `Skill file not found`.
- Real full evolution of the same external skill, `--iterations 3`, model `gpt-4.1` via Copilot endpoint: 21 synthetic examples (10/5/6 split), GEPA ran (base valset 0.564), 118.7s, all 4 constraints passed (incl. `skill_structure`), holdout 0.595 -> 0.595 (+0.000; no better candidate found at this tiny budget). Output written to `output/ship/<ts>/`.
- Bugs caught and fixed during this run: GEPA `max_steps` TypeError then MIPROv2 needing `optuna`; evolved text always equal to baseline; `skill_structure` always failing.
- Not exercised: default OpenAI models (no API key available here).

### 2. Automated Tests & Static Checks
- `pytest`: 149 passed, 1 failed. The failure `tests/core/test_config_repo_path.py::test_resolve_expands_user_home` also fails on clean `origin/main` (assumes POSIX `HOME`; Windows uses `USERPROFILE`) - unrelated.
- No lint/typecheck/build configured in repo.

title: feat(models): configurable evolution and judgment models
body:
## Problem

The evolution CLI exposes optimizer and evaluation model options, but they do not consistently reach reflection, task inference, dataset generation and judgment. The workflow also uses keyword overlap instead of the existing LLM judge. Copilot models need account-aware authentication and their advertised API transport, and an invalid oversized baseline can otherwise win before final rejection.

## Solution

Use one model factory, wire selected model roles through the actual consumers, and use typed outputs and LLM judgment during optimization and holdout evaluation. Preserve the chosen optimizer in fallback and reject invalid candidates during search as well as at the final gate.

This branch starts directly from upstream `main`. It does **not** add `--skill-path` or its test file, and does not contain the commit from #196. It retains upstream's `--skill` / `--hermes-repo` lookup. Minimal GEPA budget/instruction wiring is included because the selected reflection model must mutate the candidate that is actually judged; those correctness lines overlap #196, but that PR and its branch remain untouched.

## Changes

- Shared `make_lm` configuration for optimizer, task model, synthetic generation, relevance filtering and judgment.
- `EVOLUTION_OPTIMIZER_MODEL` / `EVOLUTION_EVAL_MODEL` defaults with explicit CLI precedence; `EVOLUTION_API_BASE` / `EVOLUTION_API_KEY` for custom endpoints.
- Configured Copilot account discovery, destination validation, integration headers, advertised chat/Responses/Messages transport selection, bounded metadata caching and existing-client credential refresh.
- Anthropic structured outputs retain their schema using the supported `output_config.format` field.
- Typed task/judge outputs without a separate chain-of-thought field; judge scores and actionable feedback remain required.
- Actual candidate instructions accompany predictions. GEPA receives constraint failures and judge feedback; identical trajectory/rubric grades are reused consistently.
- MIPRO fallback only when GEPA is absent, with explicit prompt/task models. Runtime/authentication failures are not converted into fallback.
- Full-artifact size/structure/growth checks remain enforced; final rejection exits nonzero.
- Behavioral HTTP/CLI regressions and a Windows home-path test setup correction.

## Evidences

### 1. Functional End-to-End Validation

Fresh validation of this upstream-only candidate: Windows, Python 3.12, DSPy 3.4.1. Real separate CLI processes run from isolated fixture directories with cold response caches, using upstream's existing skill lookup:

```bash
python -m evolution.skills.evolve_skill \
  --skill arithmetic --hermes-repo <fixture-hermes-repo> \
  --eval-source golden --dataset-path <fixture-dataset> --iterations 2 \
  --optimizer-model <selected-optimizer> --eval-model <selected-evaluator>
```

Each fixture places its skill at `<fixture-hermes-repo>/skills/arithmetic/SKILL.md`. No `--skill-path` option is used.

| Model selection / boundary | Exit and real output |
|---|---|
| GPT-6.1 Sol for both roles, configured Copilot account, Responses API | Exit 0; actual response identity GPT-6.1 Sol; one reflection, ten task and ten judge calls; constraints pass; one-case holdout 0.5 to 1.0. |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 for both roles, same Copilot account, native Messages API | Exit 0; actual response identity Claude Sonnet 5.5; one reflection, ten task and ten judge calls; constraints pass; one-case holdout 0.5 to 1.0. |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash for both roles, same Copilot account, chat API | Exit 0; actual response identity Gemini 3.8 Flash; one reflection, ten task and ten judge calls; constraints pass; one-case holdout 0.5 to 1.0. |
| Existing BYOK endpoint: `openai/gh/gemini-4-argon` optimizer, `openai/gh/gpt-5.6-sol-high` evaluator | Exit 0; actual response identities Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol; one reflection, ten task and ten judge calls; constraints pass; one-case holdout 0.5 to 1.0. |

The `openai/` prefix in the BYOK case selects the compatible wire protocol, not the model developer. Copilot checks keep one configured account/endpoint and change only model selection. These small smoke tests prove execution and transport compatibility, not broad quality improvement. Candidate source hashes remain unchanged across all four checks.

Controlled real HTTP integration covers CLI/environment precedence, synthetic generation, missing-GEPA fallback model selection, runtime-error propagation, rejected-candidate exit status, same-client sync/async refresh and an expiry boundary. Shared generation and relevance implementations retain the already-qualified core behavior; no private session histories are sent for this PR.

Known boundaries remain explicit: public-account token exchange requires an entitled account; live account qualification here is the configured enterprise account. Live long-duration expiry, a second installed DSPy version, and every arbitrary gateway/model alias are not claimed. A previously saved gateway Sonnet alias rejects inference despite being advertised; it is not silently rewritten or repaired. The BYOK run uses the explicitly selected Gemini optimizer. No production gate, provider filter or model failure is disabled to obtain success.

### 2. Automated Tests & Static Checks

- Fresh complete upstream-only suite: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp <scratch> --junitxml=<results>`: **175 passed, zero failures/errors/skips, six warnings**, exit 0, 44.55 seconds. The fork has four additional path-option tests that intentionally are not included here.
- `python -m compileall -q evolution tests`: exit 0.
- `python -m pip wheel --no-deps --no-build-isolation . --wheel-dir <scratch-wheels>`: exit 0; wheel built successfully.
- `git diff --cached --check`: passes. Only twelve intended source/test paths are included; generated artifacts and local memory/instruction files are excluded.
- Independent read-only review by Claude Sonnet 5.5, different from the author model: complete diff and all twelve full source files supplied, exact hashes retained; reviewer returns **PASS**. Three low-severity informational observations are adjudicated as intended behavior: selected global task LM, deliberately bounded single-account metadata cache, and user-managed custom API keys. No correctness/security finding remains.
- OCR preview selects the intended scope, but its inference invocation cannot resolve the configured `copilot-api` alias. The independent review above uses the existing authenticated model route directly and is **not represented as an OCR success**. No global configuration is changed.
- An initial test invocation hit a missing scratch parent; a concurrent run later exceeded its timeout. Both attempts are retained locally; the fresh complete result above is the qualifying run.
- Six deprecation warnings remain, including DSPy's legacy-LM transition and a LiteLLM event-loop warning. DSPy 3.5 compatibility is not asserted.

This PR requests upstream review, not automatic merging. The existing #196 branch is unchanged, and the already-shipped fork/local installation is left intact.

title: Constraint validator always fails: skill_structure runs on the body but requires full-file frontmatter
body:
## Summary

Every run of `evolve_skill` fails its own constraint gate, regardless of the evolved output's quality. The root cause is a mismatch between what the validator is given and what one of its checks expects.

## Root cause

In `evolution/skills/evolve_skill.py`:

- Line ~121 (baseline): `validator.validate_all(skill["body"], "skill")`
- Line ~188 (evolved): `validator.validate_all(evolved_body, "skill", baseline_text=...)`

Both pass the **body** (the SKILL.md content with frontmatter stripped). But `ConstraintValidator._check_skill_structure` requires:

- `text.strip().startswith("---")`
- `name:` and `description:` present in the first 500 chars

i.e. it expects the **full file including YAML frontmatter**. A body by definition starts with the first heading, so `skill_structure` fails unconditionally, `all_pass` goes False, and every run ends with:

```
✗ Evolved skill FAILED constraints — not deploying
```

No run can ever pass, for any input, on any machine.

## Fix

Validate the reassembled full file instead:

```python
baseline_constraints = validator.validate_all(skill["raw"], "skill")
...
evolved_full = reassemble_skill(skill["frontmatter"], evolved_body)
evolved_constraints = validator.validate_all(evolved_full, "skill", baseline_text=skill["raw"])
```

This is what we run locally after patching, and runs complete normally.

## Related observations while in there

1. **Baseline skills over 15KB can never deploy.** The size gate compares `evolved_full` against `max_skill_size: 15_000` with no exemption for pre-existing size. Our `github-pr-workflow` SKILL.md is 19,202 chars — the evolved variant fails `size_limit` (4202 over) even when growth is +0%. Consider `size_limit` checking *growth* against the baseline, or a configurable per-skill limit.
2. **`sessiondb` eval source finds no Hermes data on current builds.** `HermesSessionImporter` reads `~/.hermes/sessions/*.json`, but current Hermes keeps canonical transcripts in `~/.hermes/state.db` (SQLite `messages`/`sessions` tables) and the `sessions/*.jsonl` gateway dumps contain only assistant/tool rows — zero user messages. The importer returned 0 pairs from 91K live messages until we added a state.db reader. Happy to open a separate issue/PR with our reader implementation if useful.

## Environment

- macOS (Apple Silicon), Python 3.12, dspy installed from PyPI (GEPA unavailable → MIPROv2 fallback; `dspy[optuna]` required)
- Reproduced on 3 skills over multiple runs

title: Optimizer deletes critical incident-lesson content and scores higher — growth limit can't catch deletions
body:
## Summary

The optimizer can **delete critical content from a skill and score higher for it**. The only semantic guard is the growth limit (`Growth OK: +0.0% (max +20.0%)`), which constrains additions — it cannot catch deletions. This makes Phase-1 output unsafe to deploy over skills that encode hard-won operational lessons.

## Evidence

A 40-iteration MIPROv2 run on `github-pr-workflow` (19.2K-char skill, eval dataset built from 3,390 real session pairs, 376 PR-relevant after relevance filtering):

- Optimizer completed: best score 65.27, all structural gates ✓
- The evolved text **removed** the skill's two most valuable incident-lesson callouts:
  1. The required-review refusal ladder (exact `gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,mergeable` diagnostic sequence, "still a draft" handling, expected author-self-approval block) learned from a real production PR (#52).
  2. The commit-gate trap (gate the commit on the **test command's exit code**, not on grepping its output — output-format changes silently skip the commit).
- The LLM-as-judge scored the gutted version **higher** than the original. The judge evaluates whether a response looks right for a task; it has no visibility into why a paragraph exists. Deletion of costly-to-learn content is therefore *rewarded* by the fitness function.

## Why this matters

Skills function as institutional memory. A fitness function that treats removals as free improvements will progressively strip exactly the content that is hardest to reconstruct — the lessons from real failures. The README's guardrails list "semantic preservation" as a design goal, but the implemented constraint set has no deletion-side defense.

## Suggested mitigations

Any of these would close the gap:

1. **Deletion review gate** — any removed block over N chars (or containing incident-pattern markers like PR numbers, dates, "do not", "never") requires explicit human sign-off before deploy, even when all automated gates pass.
2. **Embedding-similarity check on removed content** — if removed text has high similarity to previously-incident-derived sections, block or flag.
3. **Prompt-side protection** — mark incident-lesson blocks (e.g. HTML comment sentinels like `<!-- lesson: do-not-remove -->`) and forbid the proposal step from mutating them.

For context, the run details: gpt-4.1-class judge unavailable, run used haiku-class models via an OpenAI-compatible proxy — but the failure mode is structural (the judge never sees the baseline's edit history), not model-quality-dependent. Happy to share the full baseline/evolved diff if useful.

title: feat(constraints): add content-retention guard to catch deletions
body:
## Summary

Adds a `content_retention` constraint that detects **deletion** of load-bearing content from an evolved artifact.

The existing `growth_limit` constraint only bounds how much an artifact may *grow* over its baseline. It is blind to the opposite failure mode. An optimizer can delete the runnable commands and guard lessons from a skill, keep the surrounding prose, and be *rewarded* for doing so by an LLM-as-judge — the judge evaluates whether a response "looks right" for a task and has no visibility into why a given paragraph existed.

The symptom is visible in the constraint output: a candidate whose content was gutted reports `Growth OK: -65.8% (max +20.0%)`, because a negative growth value is trivially within an upper bound.

This is the failure mode described in #200. That report is based on a 40-iteration MIPROv2 run over a 19.2K-char skill with 376 relevance-filtered real session pairs; the observed candidate passed every structural gate while scoring *higher* than the original.

## What this adds

`evolution/core/content_retention.py` compares an evolved artifact against its baseline using three structural signals:

| signal | what it measures | why it is usable as a hard constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `commands` | runnable commands extracted from fenced code blocks, normalised to `executable + subcommand` | flag/argument changes do not read as different commands, but a removed command does |
| `blocks` | headings and paragraphs of the baseline document, matched leniently | rephrasing a paragraph is not deletion; removing it is |
| `size` | length relative to baseline | a gutted artifact shrinks |

All three are **insensitive to rewording but sensitive to removal**.

Guard-line ("lesson") retention is computed as well and reported in the constraint details, but it is deliberately **excluded from the verdict**. Rewording a guard line can change which marker word it uses (`must` → `have to`), so a hard threshold on that signal produces false rejections. It is reported for diagnosis only.

## Integration

`ConstraintValidator.validate_all()` gains the check right after `growth_limit`, so it participates in the existing "every candidate must pass all constraints" rejection path — no separate promotion step is needed.

Thresholds are in `EvolutionConfig`:

```python
enable_content_retention: bool = True
min_command_retention: float = 0.5
min_block_retention: float = 0.6
min_size_ratio: float = 0.6
```

`enable_content_retention = False` restores the previous behaviour exactly.

## Behaviour change

The check is **on by default**, because the failure it catches is silent and the resulting artifact is unsafe to deploy over a skill that encodes operational lessons. If this is too aggressive for a given workflow, the thresholds can be relaxed or the check disabled via config — no code change required.

The defaults are deliberately loose: they reject a candidate whose content was gutted, while accepting a reworded-but-equivalent rewrite and a pure addition.

## Tests

`tests/core/test_content_retention.py` (18 tests) covers:

- command extraction: shell commands found, prose ignored, markdown emphasis labels ignored, flags normalised, empty input
- block extraction: headings and paragraphs separated, blank-line separation
- retention analysis: gutted detected, equivalent rewrite not flagged, pure addition not flagged
- the constraint: rejection, acceptance, details reporting, disable switch, registration in `validate_all`, and no check when no baseline is supplied

Fixtures are synthetic (`tests/core/fixtures/`) and carry no real-world content.

Full suite: **163 passed**.

## Relationship to other open work

- #141 / #184 (optimizer cannot see the skill text) — orthogonal. This PR assumes the optimizer *can* rewrite the body; it constrains *what* may change.
- #54 (promotion gates) — orthogonal. This is a candidate-level constraint, usable independently of a promotion pipeline.
- #199 (constraint validator always fails) — orthogonal; the new check runs only when a baseline is available and does not touch frontmatter validation.

## Notes

This was found while running the pipeline against real skills. Happy to adjust thresholds or the signal set if the defaults look too aggressive for the existing skill corpus.

title: Lesson probes: a lesion-validated behavioral regression gate for incident-derived lessons (#200)
body:
## Problem

#200: the optimizer deletes incident-derived lessons and scores higher. The eval set is drawn from ordinary tasks, so a lesson that only matters in a rare situation is invisible to the score; deleting it reads as "more concise". A text-retention check (#201) catches the deletion, but it cannot tell a dropped lesson from a reworded one, and it cannot tell whether the lesson ever changed the agent's behavior at all. Protecting text protects the wrong thing — the lesson matters only because of what the agent *does* with it.

## Idea: validate the test by removing the lesson

Treat each lesson as a regression test, and validate the test itself with a **lesion** — the baseline skill with that one lesson removed.

| baseline | lesion | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| passes | fails | **discriminating** — gates the candidate |
| passes | passes | dead — proves nothing about the lesson; reported |
| fails | — | broken — the lesson is already inert; reported |
| anchor not in baseline | — | orphaned |

Only discriminating probes gate. The candidate is rejected when it fails a probe that the baseline passes and the lesion fails — it has lost a behavior the lesson demonstrably provided. Rewording that keeps the behavior passes; deletion that loses it fails. No text similarity is involved.

Because a probe's validity comes from the lesion rather than from trust, probes can be hand-written (`SKILL.probes.jsonl`) **or LLM-generated** (`--generate-probes`) without the generator's hallucinations leaking into the gate: a probe that passes with and without the lesson is simply dead. The lesion is the ground truth for whether a probe tests anything, so nobody has to review generated probes by hand.

A side effect worth having: "broken" probes reveal lessons the agent already ignores, which is the case #200 was really about (a lesson that is present but has no behavioral footprint is exactly what gets deleted first).

## What's in the PR

- `evolution/core/lesson_probes.py` — `LessonProbe`, `lesion_text`, `run_lesson_probes`, `find_unprobed_lessons`, `generate_probes`, `load_probes`. No LLM dependency; the agent is an injected `(skill_text, scenario) -> output` callable.
- `ConstraintValidator.check_lesson_probes(report)` → `ConstraintResult("lesson_probes")`. Fails only on a regression; dead/broken/orphaned probes and unprobed lessons go in the details.
- `EvolutionConfig`: `lesson_probes_enabled`, `lesson_probe_filename`, `lesson_probe_lesion_check`, `lesson_probe_generate`.
- `evolve_skill.py`: runs after `validate_all` with `SkillModule` as the responder; saves `lesson_probes.json`; flags `--no-lesson-probes`, `--generate-probes`. With no probe file it only prints the lesson-like passages that are unguarded.
- `evolution/skills/lesson_probe_generator.py`: opt-in dspy generator, lazy import.
- README: new guardrail and probe file format.

Cost: per probe, one agent call each for baseline, lesion, and (gating probes only) candidate. Dead/broken/orphaned probes never cost a candidate call.

## Tests

`tests/core/test_lesson_probes.py` — 19 tests with a deterministic agent stub whose behavior depends on which rules are in the skill text (the dependency the gate exists to detect):

- deleting a lesson → discriminating probe → regression → rejected
- rewording that keeps the behavior → accepted (a text-retention check would flag this)
- dead / broken / orphaned classification; dead probes never gate
- candidate is queried only for gating probes (call count asserted)
- generated probes: a hallucinated one is filtered by lesion, the real deletion is still caught
- JSONL loading with bad lines, regex expectations, constraint integration, report serialization

Full suite: 164 passed.

## Relation to other work

- Orthogonal to #184 (makes the optimizer able to change the skill body at all) and complementary to #201 (text retention). #201 and this can run together: #201 is cheap and catches gross deletion; this one tells you whether what was deleted or rewritten actually mattered.
- The lesion/negative-control move is the same one I proposed and that was implemented in [iLearn-Lab/EvoHarness#1](https://github.com/iLearn-Lab/EvoHarness/issues/1), and the sealed/counterfactual gating comes from [rsi-metaforge-core](https://github.com/sunghunkwag/rsi-metaforge-core). My earlier PRs here (#124, #128) were larger Phase 4 proposals; this one is narrow, additive, and off by one flag.

## Limitations

- A probe needs a scenario. The repo-side heuristic that lists unprobed lessons is for visibility only; the honest default without probes is a warning, not a gate.
- Expectations are substring/regex checks on the agent output, so they test for a behavioral marker, not full correctness. That is deliberate: the lesion check makes a weak expectation safe (if it is too weak to see the lesson, the probe is dead and ignored).
- Lesion removes the paragraph containing the anchor. A lesson spread across paragraphs needs one probe per paragraph.

title: fix(dataset): harden synthetic test-case JSON extraction and field validation
body:
## Summary

`SyntheticDatasetBuilder.generate()` previously fell back to a greedy regex (`re.search(r'\[.*\]', result.test_cases, re.DOTALL)`) and assumed `json.loads()` always returned a flat list of well-typed dicts:

1. **Trailing or leading brackets in prose crashed parsing**: When an LLM returned a fenced JSON array followed by summary text containing brackets (for example `Generated 4 cases covering [easy] and [hard]`), the greedy `\[.*\]` span matched past the JSON array into the trailing bracket and raised an unhandled `json.JSONDecodeError: Extra data`. Non-JSON bracketed refusals like `[Error] ...` similarly raised `JSONDecodeError` instead of the documented `ValueError`.
2. **Wrapper objects and single-case dicts raised `AttributeError`**: Because the DSPy output field is named `test_cases`, JSON-mode adapters and LLMs frequently emit `{"test_cases": [...]}` (or a single case dict when `num_cases=1`). Iterating `for c in cases_raw:` over a `dict` yielded string keys and crashed at `c.get("task_input")`.
3. **Malformed items or non-string fields crashed list comprehension**: `null` entries inside the JSON array or non-string `difficulty` / `category` values raised `AttributeError`.

## Changes

- Add `_parse_test_cases()` and `_extract_cases_list()` in `evolution/core/dataset_builder.py` using `json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode` to scan candidate `[` / `{` spans cleanly, unwrap `test_cases` / `cases` / `examples` / `items` / `data` wrapper objects or single-case dicts, skip non-dict items, and raise `ValueError` consistently when no valid test-case payload is present.
- Validate and normalize `task_input`, `expected_behavior`, `difficulty` (`easy` / `medium` / `hard`), and `category` strings in `SyntheticDatasetBuilder.generate()`.
- Add offline unit and mocked-DSPy end-to-end tests in `tests/core/test_dataset_builder.py`.

## Verification

- `PYTHONPATH="." pytest -q tests/` (`155 passed`)

title: fix(importers): harden LLM relevance scoring JSON parsing and validation
body:
## Summary

Fixes four edge cases in external session relevance scoring (`evolution/core/external_importers.py`):

1. **Braces or quotes in preamble prose dropped valid JSON**: `_parse_scoring_json()` previously inspected only `text.find('{')` with manual brace/quote tracking and returned `None` on the first `JSONDecodeError`. Whenever LLM reasoning before the JSON block mentioned a template placeholder (`{var}`), a code snippet (`if (x) {`), or an unmatched quote, valid scoring JSON later in the response was discarded as a parse error.
2. **String `"false"` treated as relevant**: `RelevanceFilter.filter_and_score()` evaluated `if scoring.get("relevant", False):`, which treats non-empty strings such as `"false"`, `"no"`, or `"0"` as truthy (`bool("false") is True`) and admits irrelevant messages into golden datasets.
3. **Non-string JSON field values raised `AttributeError` in `_validate_eval_example()`**: Calling `.strip()` before checking `isinstance(..., str)` raised `AttributeError` when an LLM emitted list or numeric values for `expected_behavior`, `difficulty`, or `category`.
4. **Inaccurate error-rate denominator on early `max_examples` exit**: `total_scored` used `len(candidates)` instead of the number of candidates actually scored before breaking at `max_examples`.

## Changes

- Replace manual single-pass brace counting in `_parse_scoring_json()` with `json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode` scanning across `{` offsets.
- Add `_is_relevant_flag()` so boolean/numeric/string relevance flags are interpreted accurately (`"false"` / `"no"` / `"0"` -> `False`).
- Guard non-string inputs in `_validate_eval_example()` and track `scored_count` for error-rate reporting in `RelevanceFilter.filter_and_score()`.
- Add offline regression tests for each case in `tests/core/test_external_importers.py`.

## Verification

- `PYTHONPATH="." pytest -q tests/` (`150 passed`)

This pull request introduces a comprehensive routing evaluation framework for Hermes skill discovery, enabling the measurement and optimization of skill selection accuracy across a complete skill catalog. Documentation is also updated to describe the new capabilities and dataset formats.

- Introduced `evolution/routing/evaluate_routing.py`, providing a CLI for evaluating skill routing using a DSPy-based selector and outputting metrics, supporting model selection and output file writing.

**Testing and Validation:**

This PR is a draft. Merging is the owner's decision. After merging, pull the default branch into the Cezar checkout: the DevCo board then shows Plan sprint and the agent panels.
